state: Can I14 requires native JSON.parse/source-context reviver and JSON.stringify/rawJSON, exact integral numeric tokens, negative-zero floats, duplicate rejection, nominal typed data, finite recursive schemas, and depth 64/node 1000000/byte 8388608 budgets. Shared decoded integer canonical digits consume a cumulative byte budget. Encoding must bound bigint and escaped string formatting before allocation and count exact punctuation; no separate general parser, decimal arithmetic engine, or Can-owned serialization tree is allowed. Existing sealed concrete types and protected completion carriers are available; native opaque bytes now work. Ordinary generic functions remain I46, but I14 must make explicit encode_json<T>/decode_json<T> callable from Can now. Candidate codec plans: a sealed schema graph plus bounded preflight and native holder-aware adapters with lazy per-container serialization views; a complete mirrored wire tree before stringify; or a custom full parser/serializer. Candidate integration plans: specialize the two catalogue codec operations for checked explicit type arguments while deferring general inference; wait until I46 and expose only runtime functions; or implement unrestricted generics within I14.

codec.instructions: Which codec architecture meets the stated native-reuse and budgeting constraints?

criteria.native: Use the checked schema graph, bounded preflight, holder/token associations and lazy container access views for native stringify.
criteria.tree: Construct a complete alternate wire-value tree before invoking stringify.
criteria.custom: Implement a general JSON parser and formatter in the maintained runtime.

admission.instructions: How should I14 expose typed codec calls before general generic inference?

criteria.explicit: Admit only explicit checked concrete arguments for the two catalogue codec operations.
criteria.delay: Ship runtime APIs only and postpone source codec calls until I46.
criteria.general: Implement general-purpose generic functions and inference as part of I14.
